would_stop_scrolling: Yes. I landed on 'DID SAUDI CHANGE ITS LAW?' over a face even I recognise. That's a proper question, and it's about something bigger than football. I'd give it a few seconds. Then 'He'd come to South Africa. He meant Saudi Arabia.' made me smile, so I stayed.

moments.reaction: 'He meant Saudi Arabia', with him fiddling with his ear and looking sheepish. Lovely little moment, the caption and the picture finally go together.

'Three years later.' Later than what? Then 'And that contacts / led to a meeting / in Lisbon overseen / by the sports minister', over a man I've never heard of. This is the first bit that's homework. I start checking if my daughter's come out of school.

'He hadn't come alone', and there she is with the flowers. 'Both foreigners, unmarried', 'marriage was forbidden'. Oh, THAT's the law. Now I care, this is about real people. But it took over a minute to tell me, and it's over a picture of a road through a windscreen, not the two of them.
'Bend their laws instead of just marrying her. Hold on to that one.' Best line so far, I'm properly in. I want the answer.

And straight away it's 'On the money': a dark card with ~$75m, then EUR 200m, and captions saying 'Near two hundred / million euros a year'. You told me to hold on, then started on his wages. A rich man's pay is exactly what I don't care about. Gone.

(Went back out of curiosity) Hand over his face in the dugout, 'in tears', staff trying to comfort him. First time I felt anything for him as a person. It's real, and nobody's milking it. Worth keeping.

(Skimming) The answer I wanted is finally here, but it's a wall of small print. 'EFE THE BAN / ON LIVING TOGETHER STOOD' means nothing to me, I don't know what EFE is. The answer to the whole video shouldn't be the hardest bit to read.

(Skimming) The two hands with the rings: 'And he did marry her... in Portugal, not Saudi Arabia.' Oh, that's nice. That's the ending, and I'd have shared that. I'd never have got here on my own at nearly five minutes.

felt_cheap_or_ai: It's the same layout nearly every second: a picture in the middle, the same picture blown up and blurred behind it, a giant smudgy forehead on top, then half a screen of murky blur under the words. The dark cards with gold tags look like a template and keep coming back, always with more tags than I can take in: 'Reported', 'Estimate', 'Only sourced numbers', 'Our division, not reported fees'. The same tower, skyline and satellite photo keep coming round as filler. So many pictures have nothing to do with the words: the road signs behind 'he hadn't come alone', a sunset ruin behind 'in Newsweek said', and the pay-story web page behind 'The Sun'. The captions are at least clean and big. It does look careful, with the source on every photo and FALSE stamped on the rumours, so I trust it more than most of what I see. It just doesn't feel made by a person who's telling me something.
confusing: Captions cut sentences at odd places, so I hold words in my head and read them as nonsense: 'And the closed / ... / may have heard', 'One post quoted / in Newsweek said / he made them / bend their laws', 'Home was a four / seasons suite', 'Saudi clubs spent / a record nine hundred / fifty-seven million dollars', 'about six point / three five million', 'EFE the ban / on living together stood'. Dates as words are slow: 'In July twenty twenty-two', 'In November twenty / twenty-five he sat'. Al-Nassr is never explained as a football club in Saudi. Nor is who Al-Muammar is beyond 'president then', and EFE and CBS mean little to me. 'Three years later' at 36 s has nothing to be later than. I don't learn which law until about 70 s. While a card is up, the card and the caption are two things to read at once and they don't say the same words: I don't know which to look at.
comment_you_would_post: none, but if I'd seen the end: 'So all that and they just got married in Portugal in the end? Bless them.'
share_or_follow: No share and no follow as it stands. I left during the money section, so I never got the answer, and at nearly five minutes I wouldn't send it to the family WhatsApp. No one would watch it at the school gate. The law-and-marriage story with the rings at the end is something I would forward, because it's a real couple and a fair answer, and it's honest that they couldn't prove anything. It's just buried in football wages.
one_change: Keep to the couple and the law. Tell me in the first 10 seconds which law it was, the one against living together unmarried, and straight after 'hold on to that one' go to the plain answer in big words, then the rings in Portugal. Take out the pay tables and goal tallies in between, so it's a minute and a half and not five.
